messages:
jess: Customer AcmeAI opened an escalation — they see intermittent 502/504s hitting /v1/streaming/generate (hosted) starting ~02:12 UTC from us-east-2. Reported ~2.8% error rate over 10m. They included a node repro and trace id trc_c2b9f2.

ryan: any clustering info? which edge node?

jess: us-east-2-edge-05. Node metrics show spikes in http2_active_streams and request queuing on that node.

claire: can you paste a short envoy log snippet?

jess: envoy excerpt:
```
[2026-07-12T02:12:37.482Z] ERR envoy upstream reset: reason=resource_exhausted, upstream_reset_reason=stream_overflow
[2026-07-12T02:12:37.483Z] WARN request_id=trc_c2b9f2 upstream request timed out after 12s -> 504
[2026-07-12T02:12:38.001Z] INFO http2_active_streams=1023 max_configured_streams=250
```

infra-oncall: that log line suggests the upstream (backend pool) is hitting an HTTP/2 per-connection stream limit and rejecting additional streams -> envoy resets. Did we change any stream limits recently?

claire: we rolled a backend config at 01:45 that enforced a conservative max_concurrent_streams=250 for the auth/streaming tier (was previously unlimited/high). It was meant to protect a misbehaving service but looks like it backfired for bursty streaming traffic.

ryan: mitigation options: 1) revert max_concurrent_streams to previous (hot reload), 2) temporarily route streaming traffic to us-east-2-edge-03 or fallback pool, 3) increase per-route router timeouts and queue limits so envoy queues instead of immediate resets.

jess: customer needs ETA. Can we do a quick rollback of the backend HTTP/2 limit?

infra-oncall: initiating rollback for auth/streaming-backend max_concurrent_streams -> remove explicit cap (revert to 1024). Also enabling temporary route split to us-east-2-edge-03 for streaming-heavy routes.

ops-bot: @infra-oncall action recorded: rollback-config-20260712-01 applied to us-east-2-edge-05; traffic split rule added route: /v1/streaming/generate -> 80% edge-05, 20% edge-03.

support-bot: @jess escalation logged and customer updated: Mitigation underway (rollback + routing).

anna: after rollback, http2_active_streams dropped to expected baseline within ~60s. 502/504 rate fell from 2.8% -> 0.3% over 5m. Monitoring for 30m.

claire: root cause action items: revert the aggressive max_concurrent_streams change from the change set, add a canary gate on any HTTP/2 stream-limiting changes, and create an alert when http2_active_streams/max_configured_streams > 70% for 3m.

jess: Customer confirms their streaming sessions look normal. I'll close the escalation after 30m stable and file a follow-up ticket. Thanks all :thumbsup:

ryan: follow-up: create an internal runbook entry for "http2 stream limit induced 502/504s" with repro steps and mitigation checklist.

support-bot: Follow-up ticket created: SUP-20260712-098.

jess: closing loop, will add customer postmortem note and share ETA of permanent fix.
